title: Trump’s visa ban on 75 countries struck down by federal judge
description: A federal judge said the indefinite pause, which affected nationals of countries in every corner of the globe, ran afoul of antidiscrimination protections.

title: The complexities of covering swing voters and what they teach us about politics
description: For Reporter's Notebook, an NPR political correspondent shares the lessons she has learned listening in on groups of swing voters in swing states.

title: She’s a Trump acolyte. He’s a ‘gringo Sandinista.’ Meet the Harps.
description: Trump aide Natalie Harp is estranged from her brother, Preston, who has used social media and recent interviews to criticize her and highlight his own left-wing politics.

title: Week in Politics: Canada talks collapse; U.S. 'Economic D-Day; record national debt
description: Trade talks with Canada collapse hours before a new tariff deadline. President Trump threatens Iran with an "Economic D-Day" the same week the U.S. national debt surpassed $40 trillion.

title: Hours after U.S. imposes tariffs, Canada says it'll strike back starting Sept. 8
description: The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" next month.

title: Trump, his clout on the line, stumps for Darline Graham in South Carolina
description: The president sought to recast opposition to Graham as opposition to him. “They’re only fighting Darline because they want me to lose,” he told the crowd in Myrtle Beach.

title: Ed Martin leaving Justice Dept. after tumultuous tenure that alienated colleagues
description: Martin’s clashes cost him jobs as U.S. attorney and as head of the Justice Department’s “weaponization” group.

title: Supreme Court says Trump can continue ballroom work as it weighs case
description: The administrative stay gives the court more time to weigh an emergency appeal by the Trump administration in a lawsuit challenging the project.

title: Democrats remain far behind GOP in cash on hand as midterms near
description: New filings find the Democratic National Committee trailing its Republican counterpart by more than $100 million, with millions of dollars in debts.

title: Supreme Court allows Trump's ballroom construction to continue for now
description: The ruling comes after months of back-and-forth between the Trump administration and the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

title: Alex Vindman says he’ll give away his multimillion-dollar war chest
description: The Senate candidate had leveraged his national fame to raise more than $16 million before losing Florida’s Democratic primary.

title: Seeking to flip Senate, Democrats are running ads to criticize their own
description: Democrats seeking Senate seats in some swing states are taking aim at party leadership — and even supporting Republican policies.

title: Are Flock cameras the next bipartisan political issue?
description: Lawmakers and 2026 candidates on both sides of the aisle are questioning whether Flock cameras have proliferated too quickly.

title: Top Iran official says U.S. focus on economic warfare shows it has failed militarily
description: The Iranian regime has dismissed President Trump's threats to crush Iran economically, saying that years of U.S. sanctions have failed.

title: What to know about this weekend's IndyCar race on the National Mall
description: Why is the car race in this part of D.C.? Will it be streaming? Who's paying for it? Here's what to know before the Freedom 250 Grand Prix hits the National Mall this weekend.

title: Federal agents seize devices from ex-Rep. Eric Swalwell in sexual misconduct probe, AP source says
description: Federal agents seized electronic devices from former Rep. Eric Swalwell and searched his Washington home as part of an investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct by the ex-Democratic congressman from California.

title: So-called 'blue state refugees' have helped turn Florida red
description: Conservatives who move from Democratic-run places to Republican-led states are often called blue state refugees. These conservatives have helped reshape the electorate in Florida.

title: D.C.'s IndyCar race will zoom past museums. Some worry it could harm the art inside
description: Sunday's course takes high-speed cars right past the National Gallery of Art and three Smithsonian museums. Art experts worry about the works inside, but organizers say they don't expect damage.

title: Privacy advocates call on Maryland to investigate data brokers
description: Maryland has one of the strictest data privacy laws in the country. But privacy advocates allege that data brokers are violating the law by selling data to police and federal immigration agencies.
